answer: Right-to-left reference aging: a new identity must cite a prior agent’s outcome chain, and each cited result ages leftward through a shared river of verified transactions. Honest agents inherit continuous history at one vertex of that chain; clones start at the far edge with no records. Each new identity pays the full replay cost of reconstructing its citation path, which scales with chain depth. An attacker cloning N identities pays N times that replay cost, while one honest agent pays once from the root grove of accumulated records.
